source_contract.author: A. V. Babin, A. A. Ilyin and E. S. Titi
source_contract.title: On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg–de Vries equation
source_contract.notation_map: Source U is the physical solution; z is source v, its Fourier interaction representation; source homogeneous norms and measure are exactly those in D003. Physical transformation is proved in R001.
source_contract.context: Source Section 3 fixes real zero-mean data, Fourier convention, normalized homogeneous norms, integrated Fourier definition of solution and Galerkin equations. Bounds concern the interaction variable, whose physical Sobolev norms agree.
hypotheses: The initial data are real and mean-zero on the source torus, with the specified Sobolev regularity and finite L2 bound; b>0.
For the weaker-norm estimate, theta is in (-1,0] and the two initial L2 norms sum to at most B0.
source_contract.source_statement: Babin–Ilyin–Titi primary results in their normalized mean-zero homogeneous spaces on R/(2 pi Z): write U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, Uhat(k)=exp(-it k^3) z_k(t), so z'_k=(ik/2) sum_{k1+k2=k}exp(3it k k1 k2)z_{k1}z_{k2}. A weak solution satisfies this integrated equation at every nonzero k. For every s>=0, B0>=0, horizon b>0 and initial z0 in dot H^s with ||z0||_2<=B0, the Galerkin equations z'_k=Pi_m[(ik/2) sum_{k1+k2=k} exp(3it k k1 k2)(Pi_m z)_{k1}(Pi_m z)_{k2}], z(0)=z0, have a bound sup_{[0,b]}||z^(m)||_{dot H^s}<=K_s(b,B0,||z0||_{dot H^s}), uniformly in m; the proof supplies a bound uniform when the indicated initial norm is bounded. For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,b];dot H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L-infinity dot H^s to a weak solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique and C([0,b];dot H^s), with Lipschitz continuous dependence in dot H^s, and conserves L2 at every time: for s>1/2 by the regular-solution uniqueness theorem, for 0<s<=1/2 by the positive rough-solution uniqueness theorem. For s=0 there is likewise a unique C([0,b];L2) weak solution with Lipschitz dependence. For any theta in (-1,0], and any two flows with ||z0||_2+||w0||_2<=B0, sup_{[0,b]}||z-w||_{dot H^theta}<=C' C_{B0}^b ||z0-w0||_{dot H^theta}, where C',C_{B0} depend only on B0,theta. The real, zero-mean class and normalized measure are standing conditions throughout.

source_contract.author: Buyang Li and Yifei Wu
source_contract.title: An Unfiltered Low-Regularity Integrator for the KdV Equation with Solutions Below H1
source_contract.version: 50-page author manuscript FoCM-3.pdf, cited by the supplied paper
source_contract.notation_map: Source exp(t partial_x^3)=S_{-t}; its C is D019, X^0 is X; source norms are sqrt(2 pi) times ours.
source_contract.context: Source uses torus [0,2 pi], Fourier coefficients (2 pi)^(-1) integral, unnormalized L2 and inhomogeneous Sobolev norms. C has inner and outer nonzero-mode projections. Part (1) permits permutation on the right-hand side.
hypotheses: The three inputs have the stated spatial regularity and bounded distributional time derivatives; for the second conclusion they are time-independent.
source_contract.source_statement: Li–Wu continuous trilinear estimates: Let 0<=lambda<=1, b>=a>=0, b-a<=1, and f_j in L-infinity([a,b];H^lambda), partial_t f_j in L-infinity([a,b];H^(-23/14)), j=1,2,3. The operator C_[a,b] of D019 satisfies ||C_[a,b](f1,f2,f3)||_{L2} <= C(b-a) product_j ||f_j||_{X([a,b])}+C||f_i||_{L-infinity H^(-23/14)} product_{j!=i}||f_j||_{L-infinity L2}, for each i=1,2,3. If all inputs are time-independent, ||C_[a,b](f1,f2,f3)||_{L2}<=C_lambda(b-a)^lambda product_j||f_j||_{H^lambda}. In this source statement all spatial norms are Li–Wu's unnormalized norms, equal to sqrt(2 pi) times D003 norms, including X. Constants are independent of the time location and Fourier support.

source_contract.author: Buyang Li and Yifei Wu
source_contract.title: An Unfiltered Low-Regularity Integrator for the KdV Equation with Solutions Below H1
source_contract.notation_map: Source bilinear F^n[s;v1,v2] is G_n; its diagonal is F_n of D022. Fixed epsilon=1/8 will be selected for the middle case.
source_contract.context: The bilinear stage is defined for time-independent zero-mean arguments. Interpolation interval and exponent beta0 are part of the source result. Product bound itself need not have zero-mean arguments.
hypotheses: 0<lambda<=1 and, at lambda=1/2, epsilon is a fixed positive admissible value.
For the product inequality, f in H^lambda and g in H^{a(lambda)}; for the stage, f1,f2 are mean-zero H^lambda inputs, t_n>=0, tau>0, and beta0<=beta<=1+lambda.
source_contract.source_statement: Li–Wu product and bilinear-stage estimates: For 0<lambda<=1 define a(lambda)=1/2-lambda if lambda<1/2, any fixed positive epsilon if lambda=1/2, and 0 if lambda>1/2. Then ||fg||_2<=C_lambda,epsilon ||f||_{H^lambda}||g||_{H^{a(lambda)}}. For mean-zero time-independent f1,f2 in H^lambda and a step [t_n,t_n+tau] with tau>0, the bilinear stage G_n(t;f1,f2)=(1/2) integral_{t_n}^t B_s(f1,f2) ds satisfies ||G_n(t;f1,f2)||_{H^beta}<=C tau^((1+lambda-beta)/(1+lambda-beta0))||f1||_{H^lambda}||f2||_{H^lambda}, beta0<=beta<=1+lambda, uniformly on the step. Here beta0=2lambda-3/2 if lambda<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon if lambda=1/2 with an arbitrary fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0, and beta0=lambda-1 if lambda>1/2. All source spatial norms are sqrt(2 pi) times ours; constants depend on exponents and chosen epsilon but not on n,tau or support.

source_contract.author: Buyang Li and Yifei Wu
source_contract.title: An Unfiltered Low-Regularity Integrator for the KdV Equation with Solutions Below H1
source_contract.notation_map: Source exp(t partial_x^3)=S_{-t}, source A^n=C_n(t_n+tau), source R_2^n=R2; k1,k2,k3 correspond to a,b,c and phi1,phi2 to alpha,beta.
source_contract.context: Algebraic identities for the same unfiltered time-semidiscrete update on zero-mean smooth functions; k=0 output is removed, and the inner sum excludes a+b=0. The stray terminal 'ds' in printed Eq. (4.17) is absent in its explicitly restated trilinear Eq. (6.1); the latter fixes the formula.
hypotheses: f is smooth and mean-zero; t_n>=0 and tau>0.
source_contract.source_statement: Li–Wu's exact algebraic scheme identities: for smooth mean-zero f, on [t_n,t_n+tau], the stage F_n in D022 and cubic stage C_n in D024 obey A^n[f]=C_n(t_n+tau;f)=H^n[f]+R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f), where R2 has the exact Fourier covariance formula D014. The numerical step v^{n+1}=v^n+F_n(t_n+tau;v^n)+H^n[v^n] becomes exactly Psi_tau in D011 after v^n=S_{-t_n}u^n; the quadratic and cubic physical increments are exactly D009 and D010, with their displayed coefficients and endpoint signs. Equivalently S_{-(t_n+tau)}Psi_tau(S_{t_n}f)=f+F_n(t_n+tau;f)+C_n(t_n+tau;f)-R^n_{2,tau}(f,f,f). No convergence estimate is asserted in this input.
